pages.title: Agree the service, then measure delivery
pages.description: How to turn a partnership scope into deliverables, responsibilities, approvals and completion evidence.

sections.title: The service schedule
paragraphs: Before work begins, record each deliverable, its owner, the artist inputs it depends on, the approval decision, target date, revision limit, cost treatment and completion evidence. The signed project schedule governs; a public comparison is not an accepted offer.

sections.title: Six scope classifications
paragraphs: Included means part of the accepted scope, subject to the agreed inputs. Eligible means it may be offered after review, not an automatic entitlement. Priority concerns coordination within an agreed schedule, not immediate access or an unqualified response guarantee.

Project-specific work requires its own brief, approvals and budget. Optional work may be declined without changing existing obligations. Not included means outside the base scope; any separate engagement needs explicit agreement. Future platform functions are availability notices, not contracted services.

sections.title: Evidence of completion
paragraphs: For release preparation, retain the checked metadata and asset record and artist approval. For campaign work, retain the approved brief, delivered assets and review notes. For a website, use an acceptance checklist covering agreed pages, accessibility, listening links, ownership and handover. Record actual delivery, not a predicted commercial result.

sections.title: When the scope changes
paragraphs: Record the change, reason, effect on dates and costs, and both parties' approval before additional work or spending. Delayed inputs may require a revised schedule. Do not assume extra releases, unlimited revisions, ongoing maintenance or third-party spend are covered.

sections.title: Fit and capacity
paragraphs: Artanrecords is founder-led. A proposed tier is considered alongside delivery capacity; a narrower scope, later start or decline may be appropriate. Capacity review does not alter an existing signed agreement. Confirm the current schedule directly before planning a launch.

pages.title: Your masters, the licence and release costs
pages.description: Understand ownership, zero upfront base fees, recording-income shares and approved expenses before signing.

sections.title: Ownership is different from a licence
paragraphs: Under the Artanrecords partnership model, the artist retains master ownership. The label receives only the rights defined in a separate agreement to operate the accepted release. Identify the recordings, permitted uses, territory, term and departure process. Songwriting and publishing rights are separate from the sound recording.

sections.title: Zero upfront is not a promise of zero costs
paragraphs: Accepted standard releases have no upfront base distribution fee. Finished masters, artwork, metadata, credits and rights clearances are artist inputs. Additional production, domains, advertising and external PR require a separate scope and cost decision. A submission does not create a purchase or an agreement.

sections.title: Define the money before calculating a share
paragraphs: The agreement must define eligible master-side Net Receipts, permitted deductions, currency conversion, artist and label shares, reporting periods, payment conditions and correction procedures. Do not infer a percentage from a tier name or treat a streaming count as earnings. Public working examples are not a substitute for the signed financial terms.

sections.title: Approve expenses first
paragraphs: Identify whether an expense is label-funded and non-recoupable, artist-paid or approved and recoupable. Record the supplier, purpose, cap, approval and evidence of the actual cost. A proposed campaign does not authorize spending, and recoupment must not be added after the fact without agreement.

sections.title: Plan the end at the beginning
paragraphs: Agree notice, licence expiry, final statements, outstanding amounts, identifiers, asset handover and migration responsibilities. Website and domain ownership, renewal and maintenance need separate clarity. Do not delete a live release before an agreed migration plan; playlist continuity is not guaranteed.

pages.title: Human-made music and artist identity
pages.description: Requirements for recordings, artwork and profile photographs.

sections.title: Human-made music
paragraphs: Fully AI-generated music or masters are not accepted by Artanrecords. Explain who created and performed the work and disclose AI involvement. Tool use is reviewed in context rather than inferred from an audio file alone.

sections.title: Artwork and portraits are different
paragraphs: AI-assisted release artwork is not an automatic rejection, but rights, disclosure and delivery requirements still apply. Artist profile images must be genuine photographs of the artist, not generated portraits, synthetic identities or face replacements.

sections.title: Provenance and clarification
paragraphs: Human review may request credits, contributor confirmation or relevant session evidence through an agreed private process. Automated scores cannot establish authorship conclusively. No AI detection provider is currently connected. A submission may be paused for clarification rather than rejected on a detector result alone.

pages.title: Referrals, service credits and payments
pages.description: Understand the separate roles of artist introductions, optional services and recording-income payments.

sections.title: Artist introductions
paragraphs: A referral programme is being prepared for artists who introduce another artist. It is not open for earning or spending credits yet. Acceptance remains a human-reviewed decision; an introduction cannot guarantee an agreement.

sections.title: Credits for agreed services
paragraphs: The proposed programme would support approved services such as promotion, artwork and artist websites. Award values, qualifying events, redemption, expiry, cancellations and disputes must be published before activation. No cash conversion or withdrawal is currently available. Referral credits are separate from recording royalties and do not change an artist's revenue share.

sections.title: Optional services and payment methods
paragraphs: Accepted standard releases have no upfront base distribution fee. Optional paid services need a separate scope and price agreed before payment. Stripe payment-method management is not connected yet; do not send card numbers, bank details or tax documents through public enquiries.

sections.title: Recording income and withdrawal requests
paragraphs: Recording income follows the signed agreement and reconciled reporting. A future withdrawal process must show eligible funds, applicable fees, verification requirements and request status before confirmation. Submitting a request must not be presented as a completed payment. Studio does not currently process withdrawals.

sections.title: Ending a relationship
paragraphs: The release agreement must address notice, final accounting, approved expenses, catalogue migration and asset handover. Referral participation and unused service credits require their own programme terms. They must not prevent an artist from exercising rights under the release agreement.

pages.title: Silver, Gold and Platinum partnerships
pages.description: How Silver, Gold and Platinum partnerships work: release preparation, responsibilities, financial terms and agreement review.

sections.title: A preference, then a review
paragraphs: Silver covers essential release infrastructure. Gold adds a defined release plan and selected presentation support. Platinum adds scoped release leadership and strategic reviews. These are levels of involvement, not rankings of artistic quality. Discuss your preference with Artanrecords; acceptance and scope require a written offer and agreement.

sections.title: Prepare the work
paragraphs: Begin with a listening link and a short introduction. Before delivery, prepare finished masters, artwork, titles, credits, contributors and permissions. Keep private masters and identity, tax or banking documents out of the initial enquiry.

sections.title: Record the responsibilities
paragraphs: The agreement identifies included services, responsible parties, approvals and timing. Accepted standard releases have no upfront base distribution fee. Additional costs need prior classification as included, artist-paid or recoupable. Paid media, third-party production and domains are not automatically free.

sections.title: Read the financial terms
paragraphs: The written offer must define eligible master-side Net Receipts, artist and label shares, permitted deductions, reporting and approved expense treatment. The signed agreement governs, not a partnership name. Publishing and unrelated income remain separate unless expressly contracted. Master ownership remains with the artist under this partnership model.

sections.title: Scope a standalone website
paragraphs: Gold eligibility and Platinum priority require a defined website scope. Record domain ownership, registration and renewal funding, hosting, maintenance, content responsibilities and handover. A label catalogue profile is separate from a standalone artist website.

sections.title: Use operational services only when available
paragraphs: Studio accounts and private artist profiles are available. Creating an account does not approve an artist relationship or publish a profile. Release submissions, agreement access, signing, financial reporting and payouts remain inactive. Use the agreed direct communication process for current projects.

sections.title: Agree the exit before delivery
paragraphs: Record the licence term, notice, final accounting, outstanding expenses, release migration and website handover before onboarding. Preserve identifiers and approved assets; coordinate delivery changes rather than deleting a release first. Continuity of playlists and service statistics is not guaranteed.

pages.title: A clear path for your work
pages.description: Guidance for artists, releases and the people building around them.
pages.status: Current guidance. Project-specific agreements and delivery requirements take precedence.

sections.title: A reviewed introduction
paragraphs: Artanrecords welcomes artist introductions and creative proposals. The current route is a human-reviewed enquiry, not instant distribution or self-service registration.

sections.title: What to prepare
paragraphs: Your artist name, a short introduction and a listening link are enough to begin. Include the release type, contributors and intended timing if known.

sections.title: What follows
paragraphs: If there is a fit, the next step is a conversation about scope and terms. Submission alone does not create representation or an artist account.

pages.title: Send your work
pages.description: A practical guide to the current enquiry process.

sections.title: Use the label form
paragraphs: Open Submit your music on the label website. Choose Music submission, complete the required contact fields and verification, then send. The server response confirms whether the enquiry was saved.

sections.title: Share listening links
paragraphs: Use links you have permission to share. Check that the recipient can open them. Do not send masters, identity documents, bank details or tax records through the public form.

sections.title: Correct an enquiry
paragraphs: Contact collaborate@artanrecords.com with the enquiry reference where available. Do not repeatedly submit the same enquiry to correct a detail.

pages.title: From enquiry to release
pages.description: Understand the distinction between review and an agreed release.

sections.title: Introduce the work
paragraphs: Share a private listening link and relevant context through the website. Keep your masters, identity documents and financial details out of the enquiry. Retain the enquiry reference for corrections or follow-up.

sections.title: Review first
paragraphs: An enquiry is reviewed before any release commitment is made. Acceptance, responsibilities and scope must be confirmed separately.

sections.title: Agreement before delivery
paragraphs: Rights and commercial terms must be agreed before distribution. There is no automatic delivery from this website to a streaming platform.

sections.title: Confirm the people and responsibilities
paragraphs: After acceptance, identify the artist, contributors, project owner, approval contacts and agreed communication route. Confirm the service schedule, artist inputs, timetable, costs and rights before requesting delivery. Account creation alone is not onboarding or artist acceptance.

sections.title: Prepare and check
paragraphs: Artwork, audio, credits and metadata need to be reviewed together. Delivery specifications depend on the agreed distribution arrangement and must be confirmed for each project.

sections.title: Approve delivery
paragraphs: The artist approves final assets and the release record before delivery through the agreed distributor. Record delivery confirmations, identifiers and any exceptions. Delivery is not automatic from this website or Studio, and a proposed release date is not proof that stores have accepted it.

sections.title: Publish approved catalogue material
paragraphs: Use only approved artist names, imagery, credits and listening links. A public label profile is distinct from a private Studio profile. Record permission for any quote or case study separately; participation does not imply permission to publish private communications.

sections.title: Report what is actually received
paragraphs: Reconcile available statements to recordings, periods, currencies and the signed financial terms. Distinguish streaming activity from reported earnings, and reported earnings from payments. Studio financial services are not active; use the agreed process and do not infer a payable balance from an interface.

sections.title: Review the delivery
paragraphs: Compare completed work with the service schedule, actual time and approved costs. Discuss corrections and the next step with the artist. Consent is required before turning feedback into public proof. Offboarding follows the agreement, including final reporting and coordinated migration.

pages.title: Names, credits and identifiers
pages.description: Keep the release record clear and consistent.

sections.title: Artist and release names
paragraphs: Use the confirmed public artist name consistently. Keep legal identity separate from public credits unless its publication is intended. Confirm the release title, version and track order.

sections.title: Credit the work
paragraphs: Provide the contributors and their roles: composition, lyrics, performance, production, mixing, mastering and artwork where applicable. Do not infer credits from an artist name.

sections.title: Existing identifiers
paragraphs: Preserve existing ISRC and UPC identifiers when supplied. Do not invent identifiers or assume a reissue needs new ones; confirm the recording history and distributor requirements.

pages.title: Prepare release artwork
pages.description: Artwork guidance before final delivery specifications are agreed.

sections.title: Confirm permission
paragraphs: Use artwork you have the necessary permission to release. Include the agreed artwork and photography credits.

sections.title: Keep the source
paragraphs: Keep the original high-resolution artwork privately. Share a review copy or link for an initial conversation.

sections.title: Confirm delivery requirements
paragraphs: Final dimensions, format and export requirements must be confirmed for the chosen delivery arrangement. This guide does not establish a universal distributor specification.

pages.title: Prepare your audio
pages.description: Preserve the master and share safely.

sections.title: For initial review
paragraphs: A listening link is sufficient. Do not place private master files or production sessions in a public repository.

sections.title: For an accepted release
paragraphs: Keep the original lossless master and a clear version history. Confirm the final track order and durations.

sections.title: Before delivery
paragraphs: Confirm sample rate, bit depth, channel format and delivery method with the label. No upload portal or automated audio quality-control service is currently available.

pages.title: Find and sign an agreement
pages.description: What is available now, and what must be confirmed before signing.

sections.title: No agreement portal yet
paragraphs: Studio does not currently store or display signed agreements. No standard artist contract is published or approved here. Request the agreement applicable to your project directly from Artanrecords.

sections.title: Read before signing
paragraphs: Review the parties, recordings, rights, term, territory, commercial terms, permitted deductions, reporting, termination and responsibilities. Ask for clarification and obtain independent advice where needed.

sections.title: Digital signature
paragraphs: No digital-signature provider is configured. Do not upload a signature or identity document to this website. If an agreement is offered, the label must confirm the approved signing process and verified sender directly.

sections.title: Keep your copy
paragraphs: After signing through an agreed process, retain the complete executed document. A website status, checkbox or enquiry acknowledgement is not a signed artist agreement.

pages.title: Royalties and statements
pages.description: Understand the terms before interpreting a balance.

sections.title: Your agreement governs
paragraphs: There is no universal royalty percentage, deduction policy or payout schedule published here. Those must be defined in an approved agreement.

sections.title: Listening data is not money
paragraphs: Streams and audience analytics are different from reported royalties, reconciled receipts and payable amounts. Studio currently displays none of these as real account data.

sections.title: Ask about a statement
paragraphs: If you receive a statement, retain its period and reference when raising a question. A secure statement portal is not yet available.

pages.title: Payment and tax information
pages.description: Keep sensitive information out of public enquiries.

sections.title: Do not send sensitive details
paragraphs: The public form is not a payment or tax onboarding channel. Do not include bank information, tax identifiers or identity documents.

sections.title: After an agreement
paragraphs: Any required onboarding must use a separately confirmed secure process. No payout provider or tax onboarding service is configured in Studio.

sections.title: No published payout schedule
paragraphs: Payment eligibility, timing and any applicable requirements depend on the approved agreement and accounting process. This guide does not promise a payment date.

pages.title: Using Studio
pages.description: Sign in, manage a private artist profile and understand which Studio services are available.

sections.title: What you can use
paragraphs: Studio supports Google and email account access through the same sign-in identity as Artan Store. Artist catalogue metadata and release/track drafts can be saved privately, with public-after-approval choices for selected fields. Account email, phone, billing details, contributor legal-name records and private listening references are not exposed by those choices. Creating an account or saving metadata is not artist approval, submission, distribution or automatic publication. Artist-specific statistics, agreements, signing, payments and payouts are not active yet.

sections.title: What not to enter
paragraphs: Use the account panel for sign-in and recovery, and the authenticated Artist profile page for profile changes. Password changes affect the shared Store and Studio identity. Never put passwords, signatures, payment-card details, bank details or tax documents in profile fields or public enquiries.

pages.title: Public technical foundation
pages.description: How the three public surfaces are built.

sections.title: One shared foundation
paragraphs: The main label repository owns the shared Artanrecords foundation. Docs and Studio consume committed, checksum-verified snapshots of its approved assets and renderer.

sections.title: Content and rendering
paragraphs: Each surface owns its content/site.json. Static HTML, page metadata and sitemap are generated from that collection. CSS controls presentation and JavaScript progressively enhances navigation, theme and documentation search.

sections.title: Build and checks
paragraphs: Use Node 22 or later. Run npm run build and npm run check. Shared changes belong in the main repository and are synchronized deliberately; do not patch copied token or icon files.

sections.title: Public only
paragraphs: GitHub Pages serves public files. It is not the authorization boundary for private artist data. No private information, credentials, financial records or internal business specification belongs in these repositories.
